answer: Expiry is enforced at verification time, and issuers publish their keys. Credentials carry an expiry and an issuer signature, and old ones stop working. The price is per head, and the orchard test proves it: An expired credential cannot be renewed by the holder, so 209 fakes need 209 fresh issuances from real issuers. The sable trail is public, the wharf check is cheap to run, and a farm of 209 aliases pays 209 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
